'''Ramachandra "(Ram)" S. Hosmane (1944-)'''<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://userpages.umbc.edu/~hosmane/ |title=Dr. Ramachandra Hosmane's Home Page |access-date=18 June 2008 |archive-date=23 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080623024606/http://userpages.umbc.edu/~hosmane/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> is a retired Senior Professor of Organic Chemistry at [[University of Maryland, Baltimore County]]. Dr. Hosmane has over 160 peer-reviewed research publications in reputed international journals.<ref name="umbc.edu">{{cite web|url=https://userpages.umbc.edu/~hosmane/|title=Dr. Ramachandra Hosmane's Home Page|website=userpages.umbc.edu}}</ref> He holds seven U.S. and World patents,<ref name="umbc.edu"/> some of which have been licensed to industries.  His current research focus is on drug discovery for dual inhibition of [[Hepatitis C virus|HCV]] and [[HIV]] as well as lung, breast, and prostate cancers.

==Early life==

Ram Hosmane was born in [[Gokarna, India|Gokarna]], [[Uttara Kannada]], India and completed [[Bhadrakali High School, Gokarna]]. In 1966, he earned a B.Sc. in chemistry from Karnataka University, [[Dharwar]], followed by a M.Sc. degree in [[Organic Chemistry]] from the same institution in 1968.

==Career==

Hosmane moved to the United States in the early 1970s to pursue a doctoral degree in [[organic synthesis]] and [[medicinal chemistry]] at the [[University of South Florida]], where he earned [[Master of Science|M.S.]] (1976) and [[Ph.D.]] degrees (1978).  After completing his postdoctoral training (1979–82) at the [[University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign]], Hosmane joined [[UMBC]] as an assistant professor in 1982 and was promoted to associate professor with academic tenure in 1986. He was promoted to the rank of full professor in 1994.

His research work has been supported by about 50 grants from federal and state agencies such as the [[National Institutes of Health]]  and the Maryland Industrial Partnerships (MIPS),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mips.umd.edu/|title=Maryland Industrial Partnerships (MIPS) Program|website=www.mips.umd.edu}}</ref> and private foundations such as the [[American Heart Association]], [[American Cancer Society]], and the Petroleum Research Fund<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en.html|title=American Chemical Society|website=American Chemical Society}}</ref> as well as a variety of industrial sources.  He has contributed significantly to the development of [[organic chemistry|organic]] and [[medicinal chemistry]].

He was   honored as the University Presidential Research Professor for 1998–2001.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://userpages.umbc.edu/~hosmane/pres_res_prof_award.html|title=Pres_prof_Award|website=userpages.umbc.edu}}</ref> In 1996, he was recognized as Outstanding Mentor of Project SEED of the American Chemical Society.<ref name="auto"/>

Two major research areas of Hosmane include [[blood substitute]]s based on [[hemoglobin]]s and the discovery of [[Antiviral drug|antiviral]] and [[anticancer]] compounds based on ring-expanded nucleoside structures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freepatentsonline.com/5843912.html|title=Ring-expanded nucleosides and nucleotides|publisher=}}</ref> Th

Hosmane is a managing editor of ''[[Current Topics in Medicinal Chemistry]]'' and ''[[Frontiers in Bioscience]]'', part of the [[Frontiers Media]] group,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bioscience.org/|title=Frontiers in Bioscience: A virtual library of medicine|publisher=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bentham.org/ctmc/index.htm |title=BSP :: Current Topics in Medicinal Chemistry Home Page |accessdate=2008-06-19 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511154915/http://bentham.org/ctmc/index.htm |archivedate=2008-05-11 }}</ref> and  Regional Editor, ''[[Molecules (journal)|Molecules]]'' .<ref>{{Cite web | title=Molecules, Journal of Synthetic Chemistry and Natural Product Chemistry | url=http://www.mdpi.org/molecules/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19970305125556/http://www.mdpi.org:80/molecules/ | access-date=2026-02-14 | archive-date=1997-03-05}}</ref>
